description: Fetch one asynchronous job by the exact job_id a dispatch returned. Born-async verbs (Google Workspace, Snowflake, external Postgres, Marketo, Salesforce, Jira, Schwab, image and speech generation) answer immediately with {job_id, status: queued} and finish their real work later; this verb reads that specific row back, including its result payload once the job reaches a terminal status. Use it whenever the job_id is already known — it addresses one job by identity, so a second unrelated job finishing in between cannot change what comes back. When the job_id was lost or was never captured, get_latest_job searches by plugin, action, and status instead. An unrecognized job_id is a successful call carrying job: null; a blank job_id is rejected as an error rather than answered as an empty result.
embedding_description: Look up a specific background job by its job id and read that job's status and result. Retrieve the outcome of a queued async dispatch whose job id is already in hand — poll one known job through pending, processing, and completed without other jobs interfering, and read its stored result or error payload when it finishes.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: The single job record matching the requested job_id: id, provider_name (the originating plugin.action pair), status (queued/processing/completed/cancelled/error), created_at/updated_at/completed_at timestamps, metadata, plus result and error. The stored job row itself carries NO result or error column (measured 2026-08-14) — this verb reads the newest payload of each type from the separate job-payload store and attaches them under those two names, so a caller gets the actual outcome and not just a status line. Both are null when no payload of that type was written, and the whole job is null when no row carries that id.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Confirm the job_id being reported so the reader can tell which dispatch this answers. For a completed job, surface the result payload — for connector verbs this carries the user-visible outcome, such as a created spreadsheet's URL or an export's destination. For a failed job, surface the error field. A null job means no row carries that id: report it as an unknown job_id, and never as a job that failed.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: If status is pending or processing, wait and read the same job_id again rather than re-dispatching the originating verb — re-dispatching creates a second job and does not advance this one. If completed, act on the result payload. If failed, act on the error. If job is null, re-check the job_id against the dispatch envelope that issued it before concluding anything about the work.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Retrieves one asynchronous job record by its job_id
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: A blank or whitespace-only job_id raises and returns an error envelope, deliberately distinct from the job: null answer given for a well-formed id that matches nothing (measured 2026-08-14: an empty filter value would otherwise read as 'no job found' when it actually means no id was supplied). Every other error is the underlying job-table query failing, surfaced as the stringified exception; there is no typed NotFoundError surface, because an unknown id is not an error.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: On a blank-job_id error: supply the job_id from the dispatch envelope that returned {job_id, status: queued}. On a query error: check database connectivity and job-service health, then re-invoke — the read is idempotent. If the job_id itself is unrecoverable, fall back to get_latest_job filtered by plugin_name and action_name.
